title: Clinical Perspectives on Targeted Immunomodulatory Therapy in People Living with HIV: A Case Series
content: Introduction: people living with HIV (PLWH) who require targeted immunomodulatory therapy (TIT) for chronic inflammatory comorbidities remains challenging in clinical practice. Materials and Methods: We report a retrospective case series of three PLWH who received TIT at a single Romanian center. We analyzed the specific features of these cases in the context of a literature review. Results: All patients were men aged 33–39 years, receiving antiretroviral therapy and targeted agents for ulcerative colitis, ankylosing spondylitis, or psoriasis. The cases differed in terms of the timing of HIV/AIDS diagnosis, previous antiretroviral (ARV) treatment history, and the targeted therapy administered. Each patient received a specific inhibitor targeting Janus kinase (JAK), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), or interleukin-23 (IL-23), as appropriate for the underlying comorbidity, while continuing their current antiretroviral regimen based on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir ala-fenamide. Immunological parameters, including CD4+ T-cell counts and HIV RNA status, were monitored. All patients achieved favorable control of their inflammatory diseases and maintained sustained viral suppression and CD4+ T-cell counts above 500/mm³. Conclusions: In this series, TIT was successfully used in PLWH, supporting its use with appropriate screening and monitoring.
